elucidation of the mechanisms by which the activity of the pyruvate-dehydrogenase complex (PDH complex) in heart muscle is regulated.

the regulation of the activity of the pyruvate-dehydrogenase complex (PDHC) in the heart muscle mitochondria (HMM) of lean and obese mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inactivation of PDHa in obese mice is not caused by an increase in PDHa kinase, but rather is due to a decrease in PDHa phosphatase.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proportion of PDH complex that was in the active de-phosphorylated form in heart muscle mitochondira was decreased in starvation and obesity and was inversely correlated with the rate of lipid oxidation.
the proportion of PDH complex present in the active dehydrophosphorylated state is decreased by 50% in heart muscle mitochondira from obese mice and by 80% in mitochondria from fasted mice.
KAP-mediated inactivation of PDHC in heart muscle mitochondira is a consequence of starvation and is not involved in obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity is not a disease of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia, but rather a disease of hyperlipidaemia.
KAP is not the cause of inactivation of pyruyate dehydrogenas complex in obese mice.
obesity in mice is not associated with a hyperphosphorylation and inhibition of PDH complex due to an increase in PDH kinase activity, as has been suggested for obese human subjects.
